s5414: Which tank profile makes a road tanker more resistant to overturning when driving round a bend?
s5415: The higher a vehicle's centre of gravity, the less resistant it is to overturning, whatever the type of load. The centre of gravity of a loaded vehicle is always higher than that of an empty one. The centre of gravity of a road tanker with an elliptical tank profile is lower than that of a tanker with a round profile, so a tanker with an elliptical profile is more resistant to overturning.
s5419: When carrying a liquid load, a road tanker is more resistant to overturning if the tank is filled:
s5420: The higher a vehicle's centre of gravity, the less resistant it is to overturning, whatever the type of load. The centre of gravity of a loaded vehicle is always higher than that of an empty one. When carrying a liquid load in a road tanker, it must also be borne in mind that liquid in a partly filled tank can move about, which creates an additional inertial force and reduces the vehicle's resistance to overturning.
s5425: When driving round a bend, a road train may skid, overturn or jackknife because of:
s5421: Excessive speed as well as sharp turning of the steering wheel and sharp braking
s5422: Only sharp turning of the steering wheel
s5426: When driving round a bend, the speed must be chosen bearing in mind that there is a high risk of a road train skidding, jackknifing or overturning. Bends should be taken smoothly, without sharp braking and at low speed. Because of the trailer's great inertia, sharp turning of the steering wheel, sharp braking or excessive speed may cause the road train to skid, overturn or jackknife.
s5428: When driving uphill on a slippery road, a road train may skid, overturn or jackknife because of:
s5427: Sharp turning of the steering wheel as well as sharp braking
s5429: When driving uphill in winter conditions, the driver should engage a low gear or the range-change (splitter) gearbox so as to avoid having to change gear on the climb, which could in turn make the driving wheels spin. On an icy uphill road, the vehicle will not be able to move off again and the trailer will start sliding backwards on its own. On a slippery road, sharp turning of the steering wheel or sharp braking may also cause the vehicle and trailer to skid, jackknife or overturn.
s5433: When driving round a bend, the dynamic corridor of a road train or an articulated bus is larger than that of a single vehicle by:
s5434: When driving round a bend, the strip of road needed by road trains and articulated buses becomes considerably wider. When turning, the front wheels of the towing vehicle run on the side away from the centre of the turn, while the rear wheels of the vehicle and the trailer's wheels run on the side towards the centre of the turn. The dynamic corridor of a road train or an articulated bus is 10-40% larger than that of a single vehicle or an ordinary bus.
s5438: In winter conditions, when driving at the stop shown, the driver of a route vehicle must bear in mind that:
s5435: Repeated braking creates an icy patch
s5436: The carriageway surface is dry because of heavy traffic
s5437: The carriageway surface does not change in winter conditions
s5439: When driving in winter conditions, drivers of route vehicles must bear in mind that repeated braking at a stop creates a slippery patch. So when approaching such a stop, the driver must reduce speed in advance enough to rule out any risk of skidding when braking. Otherwise the vehicle may skid, putting the passengers waiting at the stop in danger.
s5443: When a road train or an articulated bus overtakes, it is advisable for the safe side clearance from the vehicle being overtaken to be not less than:
s5444: According to paragraph 5 of Article 34 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, for safety, at the moment of overtaking the driver must leave enough space to the side of the vehicle (or vehicles) being overtaken. Before overtaking, the driver must make sure that the width of the carriageway allows a side clearance of at least 1-1.5 metres from the vehicle being overtaken. Drivers of road trains and articulated buses must also bear in mind that sideways movement of the trailer increases the dynamic corridor of the vehicle combination by 10-40%. In this case the safe side clearance must be not less than 2 metres.

s5575: In this situation, only the driver of the yellow route bus is letting passengers on and off. Which vehicle's driver is NOT breaking the stopping rules?

s5576: According to subparagraph "a.a" of paragraph 6 of Article 37 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, stopping a vehicle on the carriageway is prohibited on pedestrian and cycle crossings and within 5 metres before them. According to paragraph 3 of Article 41 of the same Law, on a road with a lane for route vehicles marked with road signs 5.11, 5.13.1, 5.13.2 and 5.14, other vehicles are prohibited from driving and stopping in that lane. If this lane is separated from the rest of the carriageway by a broken marking line, other vehicles must move into this lane when turning. Entering this lane at such places is also allowed when joining the road and when letting passengers on or off at the right-hand edge of the carriageway, provided this does not obstruct route vehicles. According to paragraph 5.14 of Annex 1 to the same Law, road sign 5.14 "Lane for route vehicles" marks a road on which route vehicles travel in a specially reserved lane in the same direction as the general flow of traffic. The sign applies to the lane above which it is placed. A sign placed on the right-hand side of the road applies to the far right-hand lane of the carriageway.

According to paragraph 5.14 of Annex 1 to the same Law, road sign 5.14 "Lane for route vehicles" marks a road on which route vehicles travel in a specially reserved lane in the same direction as the general flow of traffic.
